newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul petrochem shares rise on earnings prospects.
newsitem.headline: Seoul petrochem shares rise on earnings prospects.

text.p: Shares of major South Korean petrochemical makers rose sharply in Wednesday afternoon trading on expectations that falling naphtha prices and rising export demand would boost their earnings, analysts said.
At 0455 GMT, the sector's sub-index stood at 578.31, up 2.8 percent from Tuesday.
The sector's gain compared to a 1.53 percent rise in the composite stock index.
Honam Petrochemical Corp rose 900 won to its daily limit of 13,300 won while Hanwha Chemical Corp was up 360 won to 8,400 after hitting its upper limit of 8,680 earlier in the day.
Analysts said naphtha prices had fallen to around $190 per tonne from $240 early this year. They said demand in China was expected to grow steadily.
"Although there still remain some variables, falling naphtha prices will be a big help for their earnings this year," said William Ryoo of LG Securities.
